clue.text: Garnish with leaves to cover old, ropey game?

parts.note: to deck is to adorn or garnish

indicators.note: the word for leaves is placed around the letter for old, covering it

parts.note: quits as a verb: leaves, departs

explanation.surface: A cookery instruction to dress a dish with salad leaves over something old and stringy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ropey' looks like slang for poor quality; here it means played with rope rings, which is why the definition has a question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Deck quoits is a shipboard pastime of tossing rings, traditionally made of rope, onto a peg.

clue.text: Sweet cryptic clue accepted by Daily Telegraph initially

indicators.note: the scrambled word is taken inside the pair of initials, as if welcomed in
the opening letters of Daily and Telegraph are taken
cryptic means puzzling, so the letters of clue are scrambled

explanation.surface: A self-referential compliment: a nice crossword clue printed in this very newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Dulcet describes a sound that is pleasantly soft and melodious, a sweet tone.

clue.text: Travel at high speed in pursuit

definitions.meaning: to rush along fast and wildly
the occupation one pursues through life

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a chase scene, but 'in' is just a link between two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for hurtling headlong and a noun for one's chosen line of work.

clue.text: Feature key way to maintain standards

parts.note: a quality is a characteristic or feature
Control is a key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: Describing a key method that a company uses to keep its products up to scratch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' reads as an adjective meaning important; it is the Ctrl key on a keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Quality control is the system of inspection that keeps output at the required level.

clue.text: Rotten and Vicious after withdrawing Virgin's debut for meddling

parts.note: food that has gone off is rotten

a debut is a first appearance, so only the first letter of Virgin is used

explanation.walkthrough: Removing V from Vicious leaves ICIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Officious means asserting authority and interfering where one is not wanted, an interfering busybody manner.

clue.text: Beat poet with flair to ad-lib finally

indicators.note: the last letter of each of the five words is taken in turn

explanation.surface: A Beat Generation poet with a gift for improvising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat' sits first as if describing a Beat poet like Ginsberg; it is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To throb is to pulse rhythmically, as a heart beats.

clue.text: Some buy e-book about respect

indicators.note: about signals turning the run of letters round to read backwards
only some of the letters of buy e-book are used, a run inside them

explanation.surface: Purchasing a digital book about showing respect.
explanation.definitionFit: To respect a rule or law is to obey it, comply with it.

clue.text: Second-rate celebs form bubbles

definitions.meaning: ... are celebrities of the second rank
bubbles on skin or on paint

explanation.walkthrough: Read one way the answer is B-LISTERS; read as one word it is a plural noun for raised swellings.
explanation.definitionFit: Blisters are swellings filled with fluid or air, like bubbles in a surface.

clue.text: Several months touring regressive, almost racist, comic character

explanation.walkthrough: 'Comic' suggests a comedian, but it means a cartoon or comic-strip figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Yogi Bear is the picnic-basket-stealing cartoon bear created by Hanna-Barbera.

clue.text: Perhaps Sheffield Star's revealed conclusively Simon Cowell appears to have cosmetic alterations

indicators.note: the letters are given a makeover, rearranged into a new look
conclusively points to the final letter of Simon

explanation.surface: A tabloid revelation that Simon Cowell has had cosmetic surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks the definition as an example: the Star is Sheffield's daily paper.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sheffield Star is a regional daily serving one city, an example of a paper for a town's readers.

clue.text: Privy Counsellor ultimately consumed American grub

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of Counsellor

explanation.surface: A senior government adviser eating American food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Privy Counsellor' looks like one title; it splits into a toilet and a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A grub is the soft young form of an insect, which is what a larva is.

clue.text: Hair filling out after first cut — it results in a groovy look

definitions.text: it results in a groovy look

parts.note: fur is the hair of an animal

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: growing means filling out, getting bigger

explanation.surface: Hair getting thicker after a first trim, producing a fashionably groovy style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groovy' suggests a sixties hairstyle; literally it means full of grooves, the lines of a frown.
explanation.definitionFit: Furrowing the brow creates deep lines or grooves across the forehead.

clue.text: Mournful English/Gaelic translation

indicators.note: translation here means the letters are moved into another form, rearranged

explanation.surface: A sad poem rendered from English into Gaelic.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegiac describes the tone of an elegy, a lament for the dead, hence sorrowful.

clue.text: Lucky dip bishop operated — only on the counter

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
to run a business is to operate it, so ran

indicators.note: counter suggests running counter, so the word goes backwards

parts.note: but can mean only, as in 'but a child'

explanation.surface: A churchman's raffle, sold only over a shop counter.
explanation.walkthrough: A bran tub is a British fairground game: a tub of bran with prizes buried in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lucky dip is a game where one picks a hidden prize at random, the same as a bran tub.

clue.text: Husband with issue retreated by hospital — working with doctor I start to acknowledge neurosis

indicators.note: retreated means gone backwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: an issue of a magazine is a copy
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
on means working, as a machine is on

indicators.note: the start of acknowledge is its first letter

explanation.surface: A husband retreats from a hospital with an issue to be worked through with a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypochondria is an anxious, obsessive belief that one is ill, a recognised neurotic condition.

clue.text: According to Spooner, pack journalist's car

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, as is done here

parts.note: a batch is a set or pack of things
a hack is a journalist

explanation.surface: Spooner describes the vehicle of a pack of journalists.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatchback is a type of car with a rear door that opens upwards.

clue.text: One involved Armstrong and Miller's big character — love dealing with picture

indicators.note: the big, capital letter that starts Miller's

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
on means about, dealing with a subject
a shot is a photograph

explanation.surface: Armstrong and Miller, the British comedy duo, and a big role in a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Armstrong and Miller' looks like the comedy act; Armstrong is Neil Armstrong, and Miller supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Apollo 11, which put Neil Armstrong on the Moon, was a moonshot: a launch of a spacecraft to the Moon.

clue.text: Game of golf with par broken around bottom of course

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go around that last letter
broken means the letters of golf and par are smashed up and rearranged
the bottom of a down word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A round of golf where the player failed to make par near the end of the course.
explanation.definitionFit: Leapfrog is a children's game in which players vault over each other's stooped backs.

clue.text: Joke, for example, Hackney, London's an obscure place

parts.note: a joke is a one, as in 'have you heard this one?'
a hackney is a breed of horse
Londoners call the capital town, as in going up to town

explanation.surface: Mocking Hackney, the London borough, as a backwater.
explanation.walkthrough: Hackney is a London district, which steers you to geography; here it is a breed of horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-horse town is a small, dull place where little happens, hardly known to anyone.

clue.text: Removing all restrictions on the nerd and his lab leads to breakthrough

indicators.note: restrictions are the bounds at each end, so the first and last letters of each word go

explanation.walkthrough: The middles of THE, NERD, AND, HIS and LAB are H, ER, N, I and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A hernia is an organ pushing through the wall that should contain it, literally breaking through.

clue.text: Holiday in Spain on southern peninsula

parts.note: E is Spain's international vehicle code
a cape is a headland or peninsula

explanation.surface: A holiday spent on a peninsula in southern Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: An escape is a break away from everyday routine, which a holiday is.

clue.text: Snubbed Runyon's Detroit drinking bar — it's volatile

indicators.note: the name takes in the bar, drinking it
snubbed suggests a cut short nose, so the last letter goes

PH stands for public house, a bar

explanation.surface: A rebuffed character from Runyon's New York drinking at a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Nathan Detroit loses his last letter to give NATHA, and PH goes inside it.

clue.text: Excuse one vital urge with no function

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: with no means the function word is taken away

parts.note: the libido is the vital sexual drive
a do is a party or function

explanation.surface: Justifying a basic urge that serves no purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim of being elsewhere, used as an excuse to escape blame.

clue.text: Discontented hackers succeeded, capturing heartless tech giant — unlucky

indicators.note: the outer letters plus S capture the shortened company name inside
the contents of hackers go, leaving only its outer letters
heartless means the central letter is removed

parts.note: Apple is a giant technology company

explanation.definitionFit: Hapless means unfortunate, lacking good luck.

clue.text: Heavyweight's heading to meet Rocky Marciano — one might blow it

indicators.note: heading means the first letter, at the head of the word
rocky means unsteady, so the letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: A heavyweight boxer meeting Rocky Marciano, the unbeaten champion, and perhaps blowing his chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocky' is Marciano's nickname, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmonica is a mouth organ, an instrument played by blowing into it.

clue.text: Up and about, protecting endangered species

indicators.note: the phrase Up and about shelters the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: Being up and about to protect wildlife at risk.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant panda is a famous vulnerable animal and the emblem of wildlife conservation.

clue.text: Characteristic of duvet and a sheet that's worn?

parts.note: a duvet's warmth is rated in togs

explanation.walkthrough: 'Worn' suggests a threadbare sheet; it means worn as clothing, the toga being a wrapped garment like a bedsheet.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman toga was a large draped piece of cloth, much like a sheet wrapped around the body as dress.

clue.text: Watch band making American sort of welcome

parts.note: ticker is slang for a watch
a tape is a narrow band of material

explanation.surface: A watch strap suitable for greeting someone in America.
explanation.definitionFit: A ticker-tape parade showers heroes with paper streamers, a celebratory reception in New York.
